What looks AI-made on the live site now (slop-signs audit, 10 Nov 2026), and what each direction fixes

The stage hero is not on this list. It stays, unchanged, in all three directions. Full-page shots of the live site: home · a guide article · /guides/ · /mcp-server/ · 404

  1. The big one: the site's argument, that every claim traces to a source, stops at the hero. Below it, and on every article, the sources are a bare list at the end with no inline footnotes, so the body reads like any AI-written blog.
  2. Colour: a full-bleed blue "statement band" with lime asterisks, and lime isn't a brand colour. The lavender tint is used three different ways, so it signals nothing. Process card 04 is filled solid blue for no reason, and each process glyph is a different colour.
  3. Copy: a three-beat slogan ("Be clear. ✳ Be useful. ✳ Be worth citing."). Stacked two-line slogans that would fit any product ("From a question. / To your expertise.", "One question. / One clear answer."). The 404 quip.
  4. Type: chapter headings around 64 px. The article title wraps to 3 lines and the MCP title to 4. Whole paragraphs are set in the display face at about 28 px, which becomes a wall of display text on a phone. Two body sizes in one chapter. Labels that repeat the heading under them ("01 / What is GEO?" over "What is GEO?").
  5. Layout: the template rhythm on every section: eyebrow, giant two-line heading, small blurb on the right. Four equal process cards that repeat guide chapter 03 word for word. "Read next" as 3 + 1 orphan cards. Summaries on /guides/ cut off with "…".
  6. Icons: decorative glyphs (? ↗ ≋ ↳ ✳). The external-link arrow ↗ on internal links and buttons. A ↗ permalink on every chapter.
  7. Spacing: about 150 px between chapters but cramped lists inside them. The suggestions box floats as a narrow centred card. The guide grid ends with half a row empty.
  8. Details: a giant multi-coloured wordmark as the footer (a template trope). The sign-up checkbox sits off its text baseline. The suggestions card has its own radius and border. The MCP code block is a different black from the rest.

All three directions fix every item above. None has the statement band, process cards, slogans, tinted panels, giant wordmark or ornamental glyphs. Blue means "a source" and nothing else, there is one body size, ↗ appears only on links that leave the site, and the sources are footnoted inline.

Still listed (not fixed) after the audit

  • All three: the 3-column comparison tables scroll sideways inside their box on a phone. Listing all 60 guides makes the home page long (about 10,500 to 11,200 px on a phone).
  • A · margin: the margin notes and their lines are positioned by a small script with no motion. Without JavaScript the notes sit at the top of their paragraph.
  • B · linefile: long file names are cut off in the article's file list. The MCP page links a /mcp-server.md that does not exist on the live site yet.
  • C · questions: long chapters leave the question column empty below the question (it stays pinned on scroll, but stills show the gap). On a phone the chip row and the Claude Code command scroll sideways inside their own boxes. The weakest rewritten headings are "What are the principles?" and "Why would my assistant use it?".

For Jack to decide

  • All three directions give the long guide its own page at /guide/, with its contents on the home page. Live, it sits at /#guide below the hero. Moving it changes the URL and where the home page's Article schema points.
  • "Get started" now points to chapter 07, "Your first 30 days".
  • Whether to show all 60 guides on the home page or a few per category.
  • B adds IBM Plex Mono (OFL), the only type change.
